text.p: The bitter takeover scrap between Clyde Petroleum Plc and Gulf Canada Resources dragged on with the British company on Wednesday accusing its predator of making "misleading" statements.
"Nothing Gulf Canada can say, however misleading, will undermine the integrity of Clyde's assets or of our management team's track record," Clyde's chairman Malcolm Gourlay said.
His comments followed remarks from Gulf Canada yesterday which said Clyde's defence rested on "unrealistic" assumptions.

Clyde hit back by saying the consultancy which is now in Gulf Canada's camp, used the same assumptions as to discount rate, inflation and corporate overheads to defend Aran against a hostile bid from Norway's Statoil about a year ago.
Clyde also noted Gulf Canada has had no access to data "to allow meaningful analysis."
"The independent valuations, coupled with Clyde's outstanding results, firmly reinforce our view that Clyde will deliver its shareholders better value than Gulf Canada's low offer," Gourlay said.
Gulf Canada made its 432 million stg offer on December 18 and recently extended it until February 4.
